title: Kobi <> Taryn Redeposits Debrief (internal)

items.topic: Client moving off spreadsheets due fraud
items.statement: Taryn observed the client runs the process on spreadsheets with much fraudulent activity; Kobi said that is why the client is moving to Salesforce.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Oh my god. How are they been doing things with just spreadsheets? Why do they have so much fraudulent stuff happening? / Kobi Kunasekaran: I yeah I mean that's why they're moving to Salesforce. So

items.topic: Rebuild redeposits flowchart visual with Claude
items.statement: Taryn will go back over the discovery-call transcript and use Claude to make a better process visual than the one prepared on the client side (Joyce), with the added context from the call.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: But I think I'll have to go back, scrub the transcript and get Claude to make a better visual than what was spun up on Joyce's end with all the added context and details that they provided in the call. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah,

items.topic: Requirements first, no premature solutioning
items.statement: Kobi directed that the step after this discovery call is to capture all additional requirements that came up, not to map out the solution discussed; solutioning too early can cause tunnel vision.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and solutioning too early can sometimes put us in like tunnel vision and we don't think about like the impacts. So, generally the next steps after a discovery call like this is less about mapping out what this this could look like with the solutions that we talked about and more about making sure we captured like all the additional requirements that came up that isn't actually documented anywhere here.

items.topic: Client design doc unvalidated; validate statuses
items.statement: The design document the client shared is generated and not validated, and things changed after internal client conversations, so Jumpr will work back from the business; reusable parts such as the statuses may be used as assumptions but must still be validated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And even the design like the document that shared it's it's a design document but like she mentioned like it's it's not validated. it's generated / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: We you go from like the business and work backwards and then if there's anything that we can pick up and use from the design document that she's already put together like for example the statuses and stuff it'll save us time in the back and forth like we make some assumptions there. / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: we should still validate it but the first step is to is to break down the requirements.

items.topic: Follow-up call with reps planned
items.statement: A second call with the reps themselves is expected so they can walk Jumpr through the nuances of their process; Kobi confirmed only that this is what he heard.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: we're having a second call with the reps themselves to go over their process. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: That's what I heard. Yeah. Like they they wanted to go through and like have them kind of walk us through some of the the nuances,

items.topic: Requirements in Google Doc, one overarching ticket
items.statement: Redeposits requirements will be captured in a Google Doc under one overarching epic or ticket instead of separate Jira cards; the work is broken into Jira cards only after the solution and process are validated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't think we need to create them like as separate geo cards or anything right now. The way I do it for like these larger projects and like larger features, it Google Doc is the easiest way. / Kobi Kunasekaran: When you get to a point where like you have the solution and you've validated the the process, the solution, the steps, at that point you break it down into jar cards for assignment and to work on. But for now, it'll just be like all under like one overarching like epic or ticket in terms of like requirements gathering.
items.asr_note: geo cards / jar cards = Jira cards [ASR?]

items.topic: How referrals tie into redeposits
items.statement: It is not yet known how the referrals the client mentioned at the end of the discovery call tie into redeposits; Kobi wants to hear that out before making recommendations.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And I don't know how this referrals that they were mentioning at the tail end of the call ties into all of this. So definitely want to hear that out before we make any recommendations.

items.topic: Taryn drafts solution-free requirements doc
items.statement: Taryn will put together the redeposits requirements with solutions stripped out, using analogies such as Deal Rep Assignment for how the client envisions the user interface; it will become a design doc afterwards.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So let's let's get all the requirements in a in a way that's you know strip out all the solutions and stuff. But use analogies like you know similar to dealrep assignment. This is kind of how they envision the user interface. / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, do you think you have enough context and information from our call today to start putting together a requirements? / Taryn Reithofer: Okay. Yep.
items.due: End of next week (with rough design), per Kobi's target

items.topic: Flag gaps and design-doc mismatches for rep call
items.statement: While drafting requirements, Taryn will flag open questions and anything in the client's design doc that does not align with the discovery call, to raise in the rep call or async.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Yeah. And then through there we can surface additional some holes in that that we might need to ask for the rep call. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Exactly. Exactly. Any questions that come up? / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: Anything that maybe like they've put in the in the other document, the design doc that she shared that doesn't align with what we talked about today that we might need to drill down on. Those are all things to flag.

items.topic: Taryn owns redeposits feature, Kobi supports
items.statement: Kobi assigned ownership of the redeposits feature to Taryn, with Kobi helping her work through it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think this is actually a really good one like for us to work through the process like start to finish. Like I I'm I'm going to assign the ownership to you. I obviously I'm going to help you like work through it.

items.topic: Requirements and rough design by next week
items.statement: Kobi set the goal that, if the follow-up rep call happens next week, all redeposits requirements and a rough design (not user stories) are ready by the end of next week. The target is conditional on that call.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so if they're able to if we're able to do that follow-up call next week, I think by the end of next week, we should have all of the requirements kind of hashed out and a rough design. / Kobi Kunasekaran: again, not necessarily user stories, but rough design to talk them through it.
items.due: End of next week (week of 2026-09-21), conditional on follow-up call

items.topic: Jira cards ready the following week
items.statement: The week after the rough design, Jira cards for redeposits should be ready for someone to build; this is the next phase for the component.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then following week, we should have the stories or Jira cards to be that are ready for somebody to take on and build.

items.topic: Redeposits builder not yet assigned
items.statement: Who builds the redeposits stories is not decided: Taryn, Cedric, both, Kobi or someone else.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Whether that's going to be you, Cedric, or a combination of both of you or me or whoever else that would be the next phase or for like this component.

items.topic: Payouts discovery likely in 1-2 weeks
items.statement: A payouts discovery is likely next week or the week after, and Taryn may need to scope it on her own depending on timing. Not confirmed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then we're likely going to do the payouts discovery as well. probably I don't know what next week or maybe the week after. And that one you might be on your own to scope out depending on what the timing works out.

items.topic: Rest of week: requirements plus loose ends
items.statement: For the rest of the week, focus is split between the redeposits requirements (ready early enough for the rep call assumed for Tuesday) and tying up loose ends; Taryn said that is probably doable.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we need to select the requirements and early enough to have the conversation assuming like it's going to be on Tuesday. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So for the rest of the week, it's between this and buying up the loose sense so we can shift focus. / Taryn Reithofer: Yep. Yeah. Yeah, / ... / Taryn Reithofer: that's that's probably doable.
items.asr_note: buying up the loose sense = tying up the loose ends [ASR?]; select = settle/collect? [ASR?]

items.topic: Two-week Jira board cleanup into October
items.statement: Over the next two weeks Kobi and Taryn will organize the board, close older tickets and the many items in review via working sessions, so by October old items are either closed or turned into feature/deliverable-centric cards with clear requirements.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. I think over the next two weeks, let's let's see if we can close off any of the older tickets that we have. Like I'm not just saying just you like between you and me, like let's organize the board, clean up. Like there's a whole bunch of things in review. / Taryn Reithofer: Mhm. / Kobi Kunasekaran: out so that moving into moving into October all of the old things either we have like very specific feature or deliverable centric cards that can be independently worked on with clear requirements and everything else that's like before any other loose ends comments or anything else it's either closed off or yeah it's turned into a card that we can just queue up and prioritize along with other things

items.topic: Messy backlog causes focus uncertainty
items.statement: Many parallel workstreams (operator page, player page, CMS integration) and a messy backlog leave the team unsure what to focus on; the move to Jira surfaced how much is still open.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so that we don't we're not in the se perpetual state of okay what do we focus on we have like the operator page the player page we have the CMS / Kobi Kunasekaran: integration there are so many things happening / ... / Taryn Reithofer: Yeah. Yeah. The move to Jira really helped with that. But then it also surfaced. Oh, there's actually a lot still to do.

items.topic: Quick add-operator as possible fast follow
items.statement: Lower-priority items from closed-off projects, such as the quick way to add an operator the client asked about, should be documented on the backlog and the client asked whether it is urgent or can be a fast follow. Client has not confirmed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we have like this is where you know like the the quick way to add the operator that they're talking about. Those are things that I would document put on the backlog and say hey like do you need this like urgently or can we ship focus on this and then we can do a fast follow to add this afterwards.

items.topic: Nice-to-haves after integral pieces, not go-live
items.statement: Time goes first to items needing decisions; nice-to-haves come back once the integral pieces of the implementation are solidified, not necessarily after go-live.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: That way we can we focus most of our time on anything that requires decision and then come back to the nice to haves and good to haves when we have the / Taryn Reithofer: after Rigo live. / Kobi Kunasekaran: time. / Taryn Reithofer: You mean? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Not not necessarily after we go live but at least after we've solidified the more integral pieces of this implementation.

items.topic: Drop slow nice-to-have feedback items
items.statement: Taryn said most of her longer-running current items are nice-to-have feedback pieces that could be dropped; Kobi did not confirm dropping them and asked to talk them through in standups.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: And I think most of the things that I am currently working on are those feedback pieces that are kind of nice to have, at least the ones that are taking a little bit longer. So that can definitely just drop drop those / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah, I think like let's let's talk through those in the call in in our standups.

items.topic: Taryn books working sessions with Kobi
items.statement: When open items build up, Taryn will book calls with Kobi or use spare standup time to work through them instead of async document review.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So sometimes it's like if there are things that build up it's honestly just faster to just book a call or do it in our standups. / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, if there's like five, six, or a few things that we can just tackle together, just book a call and we can work through it. / Taryn Reithofer: Okay, I'll start doing that. Meetings incoming.

items.topic: Client happy, feedback good
items.statement: Kobi said the project is progressing well and the client is happy so far, with good feedback.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we're also progressing really well with the project. Like they're happy with it so far. / Taryn Reithofer: Yeah, / Kobi Kunasekaran: We're getting work like the feedback has been good.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Details: "Kobi Kunasekaran suggested that they spend the next two weeks organizing the board, closing old tickets, and queuing lower-priority or nice-to-have items—such as fast-follows for the operator page, player page, and CMS integration—for after the integral implementation pieces are solidified"
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we have like the operator page the player page we have the CMS / Kobi Kunasekaran: integration there are so many things happening ... the quick way to add the operator that they're talking about. Those are things that I would document put on the backlog and say hey like do you need this like urgently or can we ship focus on this and then we can do a fast follow
gemini_disagreements.why: Misattributed. Operator page, player page and CMS integration were listed as active workstreams, not as fast-follows. The only fast-follow example was the quick way to add an operator, and it still needs the client to say if it is urgent.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Summary: "Ad-hoc working sessions will replace asynchronous documentation to accelerate open item resolution."
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So sometimes it's like if there are things that build up it's honestly just faster to just book a call or do it in our standups.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript. Kobi said it is sometimes faster to book a call when items build up; he did not say working sessions replace async documentation.

notes: Internal Jumpr debrief (about 16 min) after the redeposits discovery call with the client. No Jira keys said out loud. The Tuesday rep call and the end-of-next-week target are both conditional/assumed. Rule 5: skipped a team-availability (leave) timing reference at lines 186/235 and personal/performance remarks at line 235. Gemini's 'Aligned' decision on the end-of-next-week target leaves out Kobi's condition ('if we're able to do that follow-up call next week'); marked yes because the core matches. Kobi's closing 'Aaron' (line 268) = Taryn [ASR?].
